preamble: Raising and rounding of a nasalized low vowel [ã] all the way to [u], with eventual denasalization. It is attested in Lycian, where the accusative ending -ã is occasionally written -u in inscriptions from Myra, and in Eastern Aukštaitian Lithuanian, where the historical nasal vowel ą (an earlier [ãː]) is reflected as ų, pronounced [uː]. Nasalization favours raising of low vowels, so the shift typically passes through an intermediate [ɔ̃]/[ũ] stage.
phoneticEffects: Vowel Raising, Vowel Backing, Vowel Rounding, Denasalization

examples.note: The common-gender accusative ending -ã appears as -u in two Myra inscriptions, showing a local raised and denasalized pronunciation of the nasal vowel.
Eastern Aukštaitian replaces the ogonek vowel ą with ų (now oral [uː]) where Standard Lithuanian has [aː]; ę likewise gives į (gręžti > grįšt 'to drill').
